title: Session provenance and compliance orchestration playbook
author: Lena Ortiz
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines how Redwood captures, links, verifies, and packages session-level provenance and evidence during security incidents and compliance reviews. It prescribes automated capture points, minimal manual steps, retention and residency controls, and handoff procedures for legal and audits. The guidance balances forensic fidelity with privacy and data-residency obligations.

Scope:
- Applies to all production-facing inference endpoints (hosted API, Dedicated clusters, and Private deployments) and all backend services that authenticate or authorize requests.
- Covers session start/stop events, token issuance/refresh, elevated-privilege actions, model-rollout triggers, and admin console sessions.
- Excludes non-prod environments unless explicitly requested by Incident Commander and approved by Security Lead.

Key definitions:
- Session provenance: a verifiable chain of events linking an identity, authentication assertion, request context (route/model), and system actions over time.
- Evidence package: time-bounded archive containing raw events, derived session stitching artifacts, KV caches, model-version metadata, and a signed manifest for audit.
- Chain-of-custody token: HMAC-signed identifier generated by Evidence Orchestrator for packaged artifacts.

Owner and on-call responsibilities:
- Security (Incident Response): Incident Commander, Evidence Lead
- Eng-SRE: Evidence Orchestrator maintainer; responsible for collection pipelines and ephemeral storage
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: provide model-version metadata and runtime cache dumps on request
- Legal & Compliance: evidence intake and preservation decisions for regulatory matters

Evidence sources (primary):
- audit-service (internal): emits structured audit events to kafka topic "audit.events.v1"
- authn-service: token grants, revocations, JTI lists, OIDC assertions (stored to authn-assertions-bucket)
- proxy-gateway (edge): request-level headers, X-Forwarded-For, TLS session info
- runtime-kv-dump: on-demand output of KV cache ids and sequence lengths (stored encrypted)
- console-session-logs: admin actions with line-level command context

Provenance capture requirements (minimal fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_id (uuid4)
- session_id (opaque id assigned at first auth)
- principal: {type, id, tenant}  <-- stored as flattened string: "user:alice@acme|tenant:acme-prod"
- auth_method (api_key|oauth|m2m|sso)
- resource: service/route/model (e.g. "inference.generate/v1:gpt-7b-v0.3")
- action: (request_start|request_end|token_issued|privilege_escalation|cache_eviction)
- outcome: (ok|error|throttled|fallbacked)
- geo_tag: region code (e.g. eu-west-1)
- evidence_ref: pointer to associated artifact (signed manifest id)

Session stitching algorithm (high-level):
1) Collect all events with matching session_id within 24 hours and sort by timestamp.
2) If session_id absent, attempt stitching via jti, ip+user-agent+approx_ts heuristic (confidence scoring, threshold 0.85).
3) Annotate each session with model-versions observed and any runtime cache ids referenced.
4) Produce a canonical session timeline JSONL and sign with Evidence Orchestrator KMS key.

Automated evidence orchestration flow (system actions):
- Trigger: security alert or manual Evidence Capture request to Evidence Orchestrator API (/internal/evidence/capture).
- Orchestrator queries audit-service index (Elasticsearch alias: audit-active-read) and authn-store.
- Extracted raw events are written to ephemeral encrypted bucket: evidence-temp-<incident-id>.
- In parallel, request runtime-kv-dump for models referenced. Runtime dumps are tagged with model hash and sequence snapshot id.
- Orchestrator generates manifest.json (list of files, checksums, provenance summary) and signs it.
- A chain-of-custody token is created and recorded to evidence-registry (immutable ledger table).

Incident response checklist (step-by-step):
1) Triage: classify incident as operational/security/compliance. Determine scope (tenant(s), region).
2) Authorize capture: Incident Commander obtains approval from Evidence Lead (record decision in pagerduty incident details).
3) Start capture: call Evidence Orchestrator with:
   - minimal params: incident_id, scope (tenant list), timeframe (start_ts,end_ts), desired-residency (e.g. eu-only), retention-class (expedited|standard|longterm)
   - CLI example: curl -X POST "https://internal.evidence/api/capture" -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVID_TOKEN" -d '{"incident_id":"INC-2026-042","scope":"tenant:acme-prod","start_ts":"2026-02-25T08:00:00Z","end_ts":"2026-02-25T12:00:00Z","residency":"eu-west-1","retention":"expedited"}'
4) Snapshot runtime: Eng-Serving-Runtime runs kv-dump and model-metadata export using documented runbook command: ./kv-dump --model gpt-7b-v0.3 --out /tmp/kv-dump-INC-2026-042.enc
5) Lock and preserve: evidence-temp bucket is snapshot-locked for 90 days by default (retention-class overrides).
6) Package: Evidence Orchestrator produces evidence package and registers chain-of-custody token.
7) Handoff: Evidence Lead notifies Legal & Compliance with ingress url and token. Legal initiates preservation hold if required.
8) Post-incident: Security creates a redaction plan for PII per Data Residency table below, and then publishes sanitized package for wider distribution.

SLOs and operational thresholds:
- Time-to-first-evidence-package: <= 2 hours from approved capture request (target).
- Audit-event ingestion lag: <= 30s (99th percentile).
- Evidence package signing: <= 5 minutes after last artifact ingestion.
- Retention-class enforcement accuracy: 100% (automated audits weekly).

Data residency and retention matrix (summary):
| Data class | Residency constraint | Default retention |
|-----------|---------------------|------------------|
| Auth assertions (tokens, JTI) | Must remain in originating region unless express cross-border consent | 180 days |
| Raw audit events | Geo-tagged; primary copy in originating region; cross-region copies allowed only with legal approval | 3 years |
| Runtime KV dumps (model cache) | Treated as sensitive when it contains tenant prefixes; store in tenant region | 90 days (expedited=365 days) |
| Chain-of-custody manifests | Global meta-copy allowed (metadata-only), raw artifacts follow residency | 7 years |

(Operational note: evidence-temp buckets are created with region-specific encryption keys and object-level geo-metadata. Evidence Orchestrator enforces a region allowlist.)

Packaging format and manifest requirements:
- Evidence package = tar.gz encrypted with evidence KMS key + detached signature.
- manifest.json (required fields as flattened key-value lines in manifest):
  - incident_id, created_at, created_by, signed_by_kms_key, object_list (comma-separated), checksums (sha256:comma-separated), residency, retention_class
- Example manifest line: "incident_id:INC-2026-042|created_at:2026-02-25T13:21:00Z|signed_by:kms/evidence-prod|object_list:events.jsonl,kv-dump-1.enc|checksums:events.jsonl:abcd1234,kv-dump-1.enc:efgh5678|residency:eu-west-1|retention:expedited"

Legal and audit intake procedure:
1) Legal receives chain-of-custody token and validates signature against evidence-registry.
2) Legal triages whether to escalate to external counsel or regulator.
3) If regulator engagement is required, Escalation Lead requests longterm retention and cross-region packaging; Evidence Orchestrator rehydrates from temp and writes to compliance-archive (WORM).
4) All access to archived packages must be approved via documented access request and audited (approval recorded in evidence-registry).

Risk and exception gating:
- Exceptions to residency/retention must be requested via the Control Exception workflow (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/control-exception-evidence-register-template-2025).
- Emergency deviation (e.g., urgent cross-border transfer to preserve evidence): Incident Commander documents decision and obtains post-facto legal sign-off within 24 hours.

Forensics and integrity checks (runbook commands):
- Query example for events: curl "https://elasticsearch.internal/audit-active-read/_search?q=session_id:abc-123&size=10000" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ES_READ" > events.jsonl
- Checksum and sign: sha256sum events.jsonl | tee events.jsonl.sha256; aws kms sign --key-id alias/evidence-prod --message fileb://events.jsonl.sha256 --output text > events.jsonl.sig

Privacy and redaction guidance:
- PII minimization: redact user email in wider evidence packages unless Legal approves a non-redacted copy. Use deterministic tokenization for investigational copies to allow correlation while protecting identities.
- Redaction procedure is documented in Redaction Runbook (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/ephemeral-data-legal-hold-and-retention-exception-process-2026).

Metrics and automation health checks (weekly):
- Evidence capture success rate (target >= 99%)
- Mean time to sign manifest (target <= 3 minutes)
- Number of manual interventions per capture (target <= 0.1 per 10 captures)

Common troubleshooting scenarios:
- Missing session_id across events: run heuristics-stitcher with --confidence-threshold 0.7 and verify candidate mappings manually.
- KV dump fails for hot runtime: request temporary burst capacity from Dedicated team and schedule at low-traffic window; mark as high-priority in Evidence Orchestrator.
- Evidence Orchestrator cannot access authn-store: escalate to Eng-SRE oncall and attach escalation id to incident ticket.

Appendix A — Minimal evidence schema (example JSONL line):
{"timestamp":"2026-02-25T08:12:03Z","event_id":"3f8e8b3a-...","session_id":"sess-77ac","principal":"user:alice@acme|tenant:acme-prod","auth_method":"api_key","resource":"inference.generate/v1:gpt-7b-v0.3","action":"request_start","outcome":"ok","geo_tag":"eu-west-1","evidence_ref":"manifest-INC-2026-042"}
